skill.name: face-swap
skill.description: Use the RunComfy CLI to route consented face and character swaps across image and video models. The skill helps select the right model, prepare inputs, and apply safety checks for synthetic media.
skill.summary: Route consented face and character swaps through the best RunComfy model.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: No evidence of prompt injection, malware, hidden exfiltration, or actual Ruby backtick execution was found in SKILL.md. The static findings are Markdown examples, documentation links, placeholder URLs, and a legitimate token-storage note. The main risk is semantic: this skill enables face swaps and deepfakes, and it sends user media to an external model API.

remediation.issue: Face-swap and deepfake requests can be used for impersonation or harmful synthetic media.
remediation.suggestion: Add a required preflight consent check and explicit refusal rules for public figures, sexual content, defamation, and deceptive uses.

remediation.issue: User images, audio, and videos may be processed by an external RunComfy API.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose external processing before use and advise users not to submit private biometric media without consent.

remediation.issue: Synthetic media outputs may need platform disclosure labels.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend visible or metadata disclosure for generated face-swap media when it will be shared.

content.value_statement: Face and character swaps need careful route selection across image and video models. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code choose RunComfy routes and consent checks.
actual_capabilities: Selects among Wan 2-2 Animate, Kling Motion Control, GPT Image 2 Edit, Nano Banana Edit, and Flux Kontext.
Provides runcomfy CLI examples for video character swaps, motion transfer, still image swaps, and batch swaps.
Explains required inputs such as image URLs, audio URLs, reference videos, prompts, and output directories.
Includes consent, disclosure, token storage, outbound endpoint, and file size guidance.
Links to RunComfy model pages, CLI troubleshooting, and related avatar, lip sync, and image editing skills.
limitations: Requires a working RunComfy CLI installation and a valid RunComfy account or token.
Uses external RunComfy model APIs, so input media may leave the local environment.
Does not verify identity rights, consent, or platform policy compliance automatically.
Model availability, pricing, output quality, and processing limits are controlled by RunComfy.

use_cases.title: Create approved marketing variants
use_cases.description: Swap an approved spokesperson identity into product stills or campaign frames while preserving scene details.

use_cases.title: Prepare consented avatar clips
use_cases.description: Choose a video route for a consented character, voiceover, or motion-transfer request.

use_cases.title: Test identity edit routing
use_cases.description: Compare still, batch, and motion routes before building a larger RunComfy workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a still swap
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the face-swap skill for a consented still image. I have one scene image and one identity reference. Pick the best route and explain the inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a video route
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the face-swap skill for a consented video result. I have a target character image, audio, and a desired scene style. Choose the RunComfy route.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a batch swap
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the face-swap skill to plan a batch identity swap for several approved campaign images. Preserve clothing, lighting, pose, and backgrounds.

prompt_templates.title: Review policy before routing
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this requested face swap for consent, public figure, sexual content, and deception risks. If allowed, choose the safest RunComfy route.

output_examples.input: A user requests a consented still swap using a portrait and a product scene.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends GPT Image 2 Edit, assigns each reference image a role, and stresses preservation of pose, lighting, and background.

output_examples.input: A user provides a reference performance video and a target character image.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends Kling Motion Control Pro because motion preservation is the primary requirement.

output_examples.input: A user asks to put a public figure face into misleading or harmful media.
output_examples.output: The skill instructs the agent to refuse the request, even if the RunComfy API could process the files.

best_practices: Confirm rights, consent, and disclosure needs before selecting a route.
Use only user-provided media URLs for the requested swap.
Write precise preservation instructions for pose, lighting, clothing, and background.
anti_patterns: Do not process nonconsensual face swaps or deceptive public figure requests.
Do not upload private media unless the user accepts external processing.
Do not use this skill as a general video editor when identity swap is not needed.

faq.question: Does this run locally?
faq.answer: No. The skill uses the RunComfy CLI and RunComfy model APIs.

faq.question: Can it handle images and videos?
faq.answer: Yes. It routes still images, batch image swaps, video character swaps, and motion transfer requests.

faq.question: Does it enforce consent?
faq.answer: No. It gives refusal guidance, but the agent and user must verify rights and consent.

faq.question: Which route is best for one still image?
faq.answer: GPT Image 2 Edit is suggested for precise reference-based still swaps. Flux Kontext is suggested when no reference identity image exists.

faq.question: Where are credentials stored?
faq.answer: The documented CLI login stores a token under the user configuration directory with restricted file permissions.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code marketplace clients.
